subject: Intro demo & fit interview — OpenFintech trial
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara@openfintech.io>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interested in trial — transaction anomaly detection

Hi Redwood team,

Signed up this morning and wanted to flag a potential trial use case: we run real-time transaction scoring for fraud/anomaly detection. Looking to evaluate latency and cost for a hybrid approach (hosted inference for non-sensitive flows; private/dedicated for regulated flows). High-level details:~
- Expected qps: 120–250 reqs/sec at peak; many requests are short (30–80 tokens), some longer batched jobs (3–10k tokens).
- Volume: roughly 300M tokens/day across all pipelines; growth to ~600M by Q4.
- Timeline: pilot in Q3, production by Q4 if numbers check out.

Would love a short demo + fit interview to confirm architecture and get a pricing sense.

Thanks,
Lara Chen
Head of Platform
OpenFintech, Inc.
[Attachment: openfintech_signup.json (metadata)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara@openfintech.io>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in trial — transaction anomaly detection

Hi Lara — thanks for signing up and for the context. I'm Ben on the SDR team; looping in Jonas (AE) to run a short fit interview + demo. Quick next steps:

1) Could you fill the attached traffic template with an example day (very rough numbers are fine)? It helps us size recommended setups (hosted vs dedicated).
2) Which stakeholders should join the demo? (engineering, security/compliance, procurement)
3) Any hard latency SLOs for the real-time path?

Proposed meeting windows (30–45 min):
- Tue May 11, 10:00–10:45 PT
- Tue May 11, 14:00–14:45 PT
- Wed May 12, 09:00–09:45 PT

If none work, tell us a couple preferred slots and we'll send a calendar invite.

I've attached a traffic_estimates_template.csv to make the fill-in quick.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Development Representative
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: traffic_estimates_template.csv (csv)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara@openfintech.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in trial — transaction anomaly detection

Hi Lara — thanks for the sign-up and Ben for the assist. I'll run the demo and fit interview. A few clarifying items so we make the session actionable: 

• Primary inference pattern: is this per-transaction single inference (~30–80 tokens) or do you batch for overnight re-runs? If both, what percent is real-time vs batch?
• Latency SLO: is p95 < 200ms a hard requirement for the real-time path?
• Data residency / PII: would you need private deployment for all traffic or only for regulated customers?
• Evaluation metrics: what success looks like for the pilot (cost/unit, p95 latency, throughput, accuracy drop tolerances).

Agenda for the 30–45 minute session: quick architecture review, demo of a comparable workload on Redwood (short and long sequences), and sizing/recommendation + next steps (pilot plan).

I can take the Tue May 11 10:00 PT slot — if that works I'll send an invite and include a short prep doc. If you prefer a different time, Ben can coordinate.

Calendar link: https://redwood.app/calendar/jonas/30

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0187
[Attached: traffic_estimates_template.csv (resend)]

From: Lara Chen <lara@openfintech.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interested in trial — transaction anomaly detection

Thanks Jon, Ben — Tue 11 May 10:00 PT works for us. Quick answers to your questions below (happy to expand in the meeting):

> Primary inference pattern
~ We are ~80% real-time single-transaction inferences (30–80 tokens). The remaining 20% are batched scoring jobs (2–6k tokens) for re-training/regression testing.

> Latency SLO
~ p95 target is 150ms for the real-time path; p99 can be higher but we'd like to understand tail behavior.

> Data residency / PII
~ Most traffic is non-PII; however, around 10% of customers are in regulated regions and would require private/dedicated handling. Initial pilot can run on hosted with an eye towards a dedicated pool for regulated flows.

> Success metrics for pilot
~ Validate morphology of latency under load, confirm token-level unit economics (aim: <$0.0006/token for 30–80 token calls on average), and a seamless model roll from staging to production with KV cache preserved.

I've attached a small sample export (openfintech_traffic_sample.csv) with anonymized throughput snapshots. We'll have engineering (me + one backend eng) and Head of Ops on the call.

See you at 10:00 PT — please send the invite with dial-in and any pre-reads.

Best,
Lara Chen
Head of Platform
OpenFintech, Inc.
[Attachment: openfintech_traffic_sample.csv (csv)]
